description: Validates Kubernetes CronJob specs for cron expression validity, job template completeness, concurrency policy, job limits, secret ref integrity, and ownership accountability

rules.description: scheduled-job-spec.json must exist, be valid JSON, and declare name, schedule, command, and image

The schedule field must be a valid 5-field cron expression (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week) or a recognised shorthand. Each field is validated against its allowed range. An invalid expression causes the CronJob controller to reject the resource at admission time

The job template must declare both command and image. A job without an image cannot be scheduled; a job without a command runs the container's default entrypoint, which may not be the intended job logic

concurrencyPolicy must be explicitly declared. Without it, Kubernetes defaults to Allow — which lets multiple instances run in parallel. For most scheduled jobs this causes resource exhaustion, data duplication, or deadlocks when two instances process the same records

Job history and retry limit fields (backoffLimit, successfulJobsHistoryLimit, failedJobsHistoryLimit) must be non-negative integers when declared. Negative or non-integer values are rejected by the Kubernetes API server at resource creation
rules.note: Skipped for fields that are absent; only validates declared fields

rules.description: Every entry in envRefs marked as secret: true must also declare a secretName pointing to the Kubernetes Secret resource. A secret ref without a secretName causes the pod to fail to schedule with a missing reference error
rules.note: Skipped when envRefs is absent or empty

rules.description: scheduled-job-spec.json must not contain TODO, FIXME, HACK, XXX, or PLACEHOLDER markers
Every job must declare an owner (for on-call routing when the job fails) and an explicit concurrencyPolicy (Kubernetes defaults to Allow which causes job pile-up for most workloads)
